henry-james-kolbe-barry.r: NEW, AND HE CARRIES THE WHOLE ARGUMENT IN HIS NAME. “BARRY, HENRY JAMES KOLBE. BORN IN BARKLY EAST, CAPE PROVINCE. UNMARRIED. DECEASED ESTATE”, Pietermaritzburg Archives Repository, MSCE 2183/1958. HENRY JAMES is the Barry forename this archive has followed since 1848; KOLBE is the surname it has spent the project proving is the source of half the family's given names. HERE THEY ARE IN ONE MAN, born in this archive's own town, dying UNMARRIED in Natal in 1958 — so the names stop with him. He is the third Barry found carrying Kolbe as a forename, after Richard Pieter Kolbe Barry and Anton Rector Kolbe Barry. NO PARENTS NAMED; the estate is not read.

margrith-louisa-maria-barry.v: Margreth Louisa Mary — and the index gives her no surname at all
margrith-louisa-maria-barry.r: ONE OF THE TWO MISSING BARRY CHILDREN, FOUND 16 SEPTEMBER 2026 — and open question 13 has been asking for her since this site was written. The 1903 registration of her father's death says ELEVEN children; his own death notice names eight and her mother's names nine. SHE IS IN THE BURGERSDORP REGISTER AND NOT IN ANY NAME SEARCH, BECAUSE THE INDEX GIVES HER NO SURNAME: two separate index passes of the same page read “MARGRITH LOUISA MARIA” and “MARGRETH LOUISA MARY”, and the Name column stops there. It is the blank Name column again, the same failure that hid her sister Catherine Mary Sophia of 1855. Found by asking the index for a RELATIONSHIP — father John Barry, mother a Kolbe — and letting it return whatever the child was called. Her parents are entered as “Margrith Willemina Kolbe + John Barry”. SHE IS ALMOST CERTAINLY THE “MARGARET MARY” NAMED ON HER PARENTS' DEATH NOTICES AND NEVER PLACED: it is her mother's name, and there is no other candidate in the sibling group. ark:/61903/1:1:6VYG-SS94 and 1:1:6F4L-76PK.

hits.text: Nine baptisms come back for the couple, and TWO OF THEM WERE NOT IN THIS ARCHIVE. william-frederick-thomas-barry.r: THE OTHER MISSING BARRY CHILD, AND HE IS INVISIBLE FOR THE OPPOSITE REASON TO HIS SISTER. She has no surname in the index; HE HAS THE SAME NAME AS HIS BROTHER. William Fredrik Barry was born 23 August 1853 and baptised at Burgersdorp; this William Frederick Thomas was born 29 SEPTEMBER 1861 and baptised at GRAAFF-REINET, eight years later, to the same parents — “Margaret Wilhelmina Kolbe + John Barry”. A SEARCH FOR WILLIAM BARRY RETURNS THE 1853 CHILD AND STOPS, and nothing in the result says there is a second. BY THIS FAMILY'S OWN PRACTICE THE FIRST WILLIAM MUST HAVE DIED — a baptism is not done twice, which is exactly what this archive concluded about the two Catherine Mary Sophias. The “WILLIAM who appears on nothing else” on his mother's death notice is one of these two and the notice does not say which. ark:/61903/1:1:623R-9MM9 and 1:1:62GJ-SD8Z.

catherine-mary-sophia-barry-of-1855.r: THE TENTH CHILD, FOUND BY READING 267 REGISTER IMAGES — and she has the same name as her sister. Burgersdorp doopregister, image group 008039088, image 427: born 10 JULY 1855, baptised 22 JULY 1855, father JOHN BARRY, mother MARGARET LOUISA KOLBE. FOUR YEARS LATER THE SAME PARENTS BAPTISED ANOTHER CATHARINA MARY SOPHIA at Dordrecht, born 4 August 1859 — the woman who married into the Booyzens and carried the name to Australia. TWO DAUGHTERS, ONE NAME, DIFFERENT BIRTHDAYS FOUR YEARS APART IN DIFFERENT TOWNS. A baptism is not done twice, so the ordinary reading is the ordinary Cape practice: THIS CHILD DIED, AND THE NAME WAS GIVEN AGAIN. This archive has no burial for her and states the death only as “before August 1859”. AND SHE EXPLAINS THE NAME TWICE OVER: the archive has already shown CATHERINE MARIA SOPHIA is a Kolbe name, off the 1848 godmother Catharine Sophia Maria Kolber. It was thought important enough to use, lose, and use again.

george-augustus-kolbe-of-bethulie.r: TAKEN PRISONER IN 1901, AGED 32, AT STERKFONTEIN IN THE BETHULIE DISTRICT, AND RECORDED AS A FREE STATER. TNA WO 108/368 folio 581. Sent to Natal. THE SECOND MAN OF THAT NAME IN THE SAME LIST — the first being GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE OF BURGERSDORP, whom this archive identified from the Wakkerstroom stones. Bethulie is on the Orange River, in the country the Settler preached across. AND THIRTEEN YEARS LATER A G. A. KOLBE OF BETHULIE IS PRESIDENT OF THE ORANGE FREE STATE AGRICULTURAL ASSOCIATION. The British press, 26 June to 22 July 1914: “MR. G. A. KOLBE (BETHULIE)” in the delegate list printed by the Daily Telegraph; “MR G. A. KOLBE, PRESIDENT OF THE ORANGE FREE STATE AGRICULTURAL ASSOCIATION AND CHAIRMAN OF THE ORANGE FREE STATE DELEGATION” at the Royal Agricultural Society’s show, in the Western Daily Press, Dundee Courier, Cork Free Press and Exeter and Plymouth Gazette of 2 July; and on 22 July the Daily Malta Chronicle has him sending A TELEGRAM OF RESPECTFUL GREETING TO QUEEN WILHELMINA on the delegation’s behalf. SAME INITIALS, SAME DISTRICT, THIRTEEN YEARS APART — from a prisoner’s number to the head of the Free State’s farmers. NO DESCENT FROM THE SETTLER IS CLAIMED HERE.

andries-frederick-kolbe-of-leeuwberg.r: TAKEN PRISONER IN 1901, AGED 45, AT LEEUWBERG IN THE BLOEMFONTEIN DISTRICT. TNA WO 108/368 folio 431. Sent to Cape Town and Natal. LEEUWBERG IS THE FARM COMMANDANT JOHN GERSON ELIEZAR KOLBE DIED ON, on 3 April 1868, of typhus caught on commando, leaving a widow and TWELVE CHILDREN — EIGHT SONS AND FOUR DAUGHTERS, of whom this archive can put a hand on two. THIRTY-THREE YEARS LATER A KOLBE IS STILL FARMING IT. Born about 1856, this man would have been twelve when the Commandant died, and he sits inside the age bracket of those eight sons. The farm also carries the Jephts of the 1868 horse-theft case. NO DESCENT IS DOCUMENTED AND NONE IS CLAIMED HERE — what is documented is a farm, a surname and a date. The paper that would settle it is VAB MHG M777, the 1896 estate of the Commandant’s widow ANNA JACOBA VAN DER MERWE, filed under her second husband’s name McCABE, WHICH WOULD NAME ALL TWELVE CHILDREN. Identified, unread, in Bloemfontein.
andries-frederick-kolbe-of-leeuwberg.tree: That he is one of the Commandant’s eight sons. It rests on the farm, the surname and his age, and on nothing else.

a-werdmuller-child-of-1857.r: AND BY THE AFTERNOON THERE WAS A CANDIDATE FOR THE MISSING NAME. The Queenstown Free Press of 13 February 1884 marries “CHARLES ANDREW WERDMULLER, OF STEYNSBURG, SECOND SON OF THE LATE C.J.O. WERDMULLER, OF BURGHERSDORP” to Charlotte Anne Callaghan. A man born 14 February 1857 was twenty-seven that week. NOT PROVED: no document read here names Charles Andrew’s mother, and his father — or a man of exactly that name — married again at Burgersdorp in 1874. NAMELESS IN THE INDEX, AND THAT IS THE POINT. The same sweep that found the tenth Barry child turned up a second entry with an EMPTY NAME COLUMN: born 14 February 1857, baptised 10 April 1857 at Burgersdorp, mother AUGUSTA LOUISA KOLBE, father COENRAAD JOHANNES OTTO WERDMULLER. She is the Settler's fourth daughter, born at Graaff-Reinet in 1829 — and this is the first of her children this archive has ever seen. THE CHILD'S OWN NAME IS ON THE PAGE AND NOT IN THE INDEX, so no search will ever return it. The register image has not been read; only the index line.

g-a-kolbe-of-piet-retief.v: almost certainly GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE, the Settler's twin son
g-a-kolbe-of-piet-retief.r: A DATE FOR THE TWIN, IF IT IS HIM. The stone at PIET RETIEF reads “VADER EN MOEDER — G.A. KOLBE — GEB. 23 FEB. 1836 — OVERL. 7 JAN. 1913 — A.M. KOLBE — GEB. 4 MEI 1843 — OVERL. 21 SEP. 1907 — VAN HUN KINDERS”. The Settler's ninth and tenth children were TWINS born at BURGERSDORP IN 1836, Charlotte Felicia and George Augustus, and this archive has never had a day for either. A G.A. KOLBE BORN 23 FEBRUARY 1836 IS EXACTLY THE RIGHT MAN IN EXACTLY THE RIGHT YEAR — and it would date his twin sister too. IT IS INITIALS AND A YEAR, NOT A NAME AND A PARENT, and this archive has spent today being careful about exactly this. It would also give the OTHER George Augustus Kolbe — born Burgersdorp 2 October 1861, dead Standerton 1934, buried Wakkerstroom — a plausible father aged twenty-five, which is the shape the eastern Transvaal Kolbes have been missing.

john-gerson-eliezar-kolbe.v: “Jan” · JOHN GERSON ELIEZER KOLBE, in his obituary · Commandant Kolbe
john-gerson-eliezar-kolbe.r: THE SETTLER'S ELDEST CHILD, AND UNTIL TODAY A LINE IN A TABLE. His obituary — Grahamstown Journal, 15 April 1868, headed “DEATH OF COMMANDANT KOLBE” — gives the whole man. Born 7 JULY 1822; married 3 APRIL 1843 to ANNA JACOBA VAN DER MERWE; DIED 3 APRIL 1868, ON HIS WEDDING ANNIVERSARY, at the farm LEEUWBERG, of TYPHUS OR TYPHOID CAUGHT ON COMMANDO — “thus adding another to the long list of victims of our miserable war”. He had settled on KAALSPRUIT about 1850 and lies there — AND HE CONFIRMS THE FARM HIMSELF. A lost-property advertisement he placed in the Friend on 9 MARCH 1864 is signed “J.G.E. KOLBE, Kafferberg, Kaalspruit” (the address as the paper printed it). The Friend’s own obituary transcription reads “[Randspruit]”, bracketed by the transcriber as doubtful; the man’s own address settles it. THAT ADVERTISEMENT ALSO PUTS THE TWO BROTHERS IN ONE DOCUMENT: it concerns “a promissory note, date 9th March 1864, drawn by GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE in favor of J.G.E. KOLBE, payable 4 months after date for £154 Stg” — lost on the Market Square at Bloemfontein. HE LEFT A WIDOW AND TWELVE CHILDREN — “OF THE EIGHT SONS AND FOUR DAUGHTERS HE HAS LEFT BEHIND HIM”, which is the Friend of the Free State’s own wording and a count the Grahamstown reprint drops. Only one daughter was married and the youngest child was an infant; TWO SONS HAD BEEN SERVING WITH HIM IN THE FIELD and “proved themselves amongst the bravest of our burghers”. NONE OF THE TWELVE IS NAMED AND NONE IS IN THIS ARCHIVE. He was COMMANDANT OF THE DISTRICT, A JUSTICE OF THE PEACE, A DIRECTOR OF THE BLOEMFONTEIN BANK and a DEACON of the Dutch Reformed Church, and he had spoken in the VOLKSRAAD in May 1867. He had refused public life for twelve years after THE ABANDONMENT, having protested the British withdrawal and applied to SIR GEORGE CLERK for compensation for his land so that he might leave with the troops; failing that, “he, like many more, had to cast his lot with the Free State”. AND ON HIS DEATHBED, in full possession of his senses, he told the doctor and the others present THAT THIS STATE HAD TAKEN TOO MUCH LAND FROM THE BASUTOS, that he had always thought so and had said so in the Raad, and begged them to rescind the resolution and treat with the Governor for an equitable boundary.

francis-mccabe.d: 23 Feb 1872, the Modder River road, district Bloemfontein
francis-mccabe.r: THE SECOND HUSBAND, and the reason the Commandant's widow is filed under the wrong surname in the Free State estate index. LANDDROST OF BLOEMFONTEIN, son of DR PATRICK McCABE, a Staff-Assistant Surgeon attached to the British Army on the Cape Frontier; his mother ROSE died at Bloemfontein on 1 August 1858, aged 72 years 3 months and 8 days. He married Anna Jacoba van der Merwe about APRIL 1871 — “his second wife, about ten months since” — and was dead within fifteen months. ON THE ANNIVERSARY OF THE STATE'S INDEPENDENCE he had spent the day superintending the burghers' annual target shooting for the government prize; at a quarter past five he set off by spring-cart for the Diamond Fields meaning to sleep at his own farm “UITVLUGT” on the Modder River; at about half past seven, in deceptive moonlight and one hour's ride short of the farm of G.F. Enslin, the cart went into a sluit washed out by the rains. He was dead of heart disease that evening. HE LEFT FOUR SONS AND TWO DAUGHTERS OF HIS OWN AND “A LARGE FAMILY OF STEP-CHILDREN”, which is a newspaper counting the Commandant's twelve. His brother JOSEPH, the well-known trader and traveller, had died in the interior in December 1865; his brother JOHN died at Bloemfontein in 1860. He was buried on the Sunday afternoon at six o'clock, the coffin carried by the resident members of the Volksraad and the principal government officers, with the State President and upwards of two hundred walking behind. 15 SEPTEMBER, FROM THE FREE STATE ESTATE INDEX. VAB MHG C129: “MCCABE, FRANCIS. EGGENOTES 1) MARIA PETRONELLA ELISABETHA ANTOINETTA RAATH EN 2) ANNA (GEBORE VAN DER MERWE)”, 1872 — SO HE HAD A FIRST WIFE AND SHE HAS A NAME. And VAB 1/3/1/12 BC11: “MCCABE, FRANCIS. INSOLVENTE BOEDEL”, with the remark “BEVAT GEEN STERFKENNIS NIE” — CONTAINS NO DEATH NOTICE. The Landdrost of Bloemfontein, buried with the State President walking behind him and two hundred people after that, LEFT AN INSOLVENT ESTATE. His widow's own entry, M777, names both her husbands, so the remarriage is in the archives and not only in a newspaper.

anna-jacoba-van-der-merwe.r: SHE REMARRIED, AND HER SECOND HUSBAND IS WHY SHE WAS HARD TO FIND. The Free State archives hold her under a different surname: VAB MHG M777 — “MCCABE, ANNA JACOBA. NOOIENSVAN VAN DER MERWE. EGGENOTE JOHN GHERSON [KOLBE]”, 1896. WIDOWED IN 1868 WITH TWELVE CHILDREN AND DEAD TWENTY-EIGHT YEARS LATER AS MRS MCCABE. Her husband’s own estate is beside it — VAB MHG K71, “KOLBE, JOHN GERSON ELEAZAR. EGGENOTE ANNA JACOBA (GEBORE VAN DER MERWE)”, 1868. AND THE McCABE NAME IS ALREADY IN THIS ARCHIVE: a ROSA MAGDALENA KOLBE was baptised at Bloemfontein in 1890 to Frederik Fortuna Kolbe and MARIA PETRONELLA ELIZABETH ANTOINETTA MCCABE — a second Kolbe–McCabe marriage in the same small Free State world, and this archive does not yet know whether that is a coincidence. NEITHER ESTATE IS READ. M777 is the document that would name the twelve children. Married JOHN GERSON ELIEZAR KOLBE on 3 APRIL 1843 and was widowed on the same date twenty-five years later. She is the third van der Merwe to marry into these families. 15 SEPTEMBER 2026 — McCABE HAS A FIRST NAME, A BIRTH DATE AND AN OFFICE. He is FRANCIS McCABE, LANDDROST OF BLOEMFONTEIN, son of Dr Patrick McCabe, a Staff-Assistant Surgeon attached to the British Army on the Cape Frontier, born at one of the military posts in what is now British Kaffraria on 29 SEPTEMBER 1817. His obituary in The Friend says he “married his second wife about ten months since — THE WIDOW OF THE LATE COMMANDANT J.G.E. KOLBE, OF KAFIRBERG, NEAR THIS TOWN”, and he died suddenly of heart disease on the Modder River road on 23 FEBRUARY 1872, aged 54, leaving “a widow, four sons and two daughters, BESIDES A LARGE FAMILY OF STEP-CHILDREN”. SO: MARRIED 3 APRIL 1843, WIDOWED 3 APRIL 1868 WITH TWELVE CHILDREN, MARRIED AGAIN ABOUT APRIL 1871, WIDOWED AGAIN FIFTEEN MONTHS LATER, AND DEAD IN 1896 UNDER HIS NAME. For about eleven months there were eighteen children attached to one household. She was living at SPRINGFIELD, WARD UPPER MODDER-RIVER, DISTRICT BLOEMFONTEIN in October 1868, when a black mare and foal of hers were stolen — the court record that says so is the only document this archive has that shows her doing anything at all.

coenraad-johannes-otto-werdmuller.d: 1882 — death notice KAB MOOC 6/9/187, 4160; will MOOC 7/1/431, 102
coenraad-johannes-otto-werdmuller.r: HE IS IN THE CAPE ARCHIVES FROM 1854 TO 1882 AND HE DIED IN 1882, not merely “before February 1884”. Motions in the Supreme Court in 1854, 1855, 1872 and 1873; a trustee in other men’s insolvent estates; and in 1882, GSC 2/1/1/41 no. 60, “CHARLES ANDREW WERDMULLER AND COENRAAD JOHANNES OTTO WERDMULLER TRADING AS C.A. WERDMULLER AND COMPANY” — FATHER AND SON IN BUSINESS TOGETHER, in the year he died. His own death notice and will are both filed and neither is read. THE MAN THE SETTLER’S FOURTH DAUGHTER MARRIED, and until today a bracket after her name. He is at BURGERSDORP in April 1857, standing at a font with AUGUSTA LOUISA KOLBE. He is at Burgersdorp again on 7 JULY 1874, married BY SPECIAL LICENCE by the Rev. William Cromar to ELIZABETH JOHANNA CATHARINE VORSTER — and the Eastern Province Herald prints his name in full as COENRAAD JOHANNES OTTO WERDMULLER D’ELGG, which is the first time this archive has seen the von Elgg written by anyone but a genealogist. He is DEAD by February 1884, when his second son marries as the son of “the late C.J.O. Werdmuller of Burghersdorp”. WHETHER AUGUSTA LOUISA WAS DEAD BEFORE 1874 THIS ARCHIVE DOES NOT KNOW.

charles-andrew-werdmuller.r: THE DATES NOW CLOSE AROUND HIM, THOUGH NO DOCUMENT YET NAMES HIS MOTHER. His father’s first wife, AUGUSTA LOUISA KOLBE, MADE A WILL IN 1868 AND DIED IN 1873 — KAB MOOC 7/1/332 no. 205, “KOLBE, AUGUSTA LOUISA, WIFE OF COENRAAD JOHANNES OTTO WERDMULLER VAN ELGG”, filed 1873 — and his father remarried on 7 JULY 1874. IN 1882 CHARLES ANDREW WAS IN BUSINESS WITH HIS FATHER as C.A. Werdmuller and Company, and in February 1884 he married. A SON OF THE 1874 MARRIAGE WOULD HAVE BEEN SEVEN AND NINE. He can only be a child of the first marriage, and the first wife is the Settler’s daughter. THE ONE LOOPHOLE LEFT is an earlier wife before Augusta Louisa, and his father’s 1882 DEATH NOTICE would close it by naming the children. SECOND SON OF THE LATE C.J.O. WERDMULLER OF BURGHERSDORP, married at Wesley Church, Queenstown, on 13 FEBRUARY 1884 to CHARLOTTE ANNE CALLAGHAN, eldest daughter of Hugh Callaghan of Ashby Manor. Of STEYNSBURG then, and by 1909 CHARLES WERDMULLER, J.P., OF HOOPSTAD in the Orange River Colony — the town his wife died in. HIS MOTHER IS NOT NAMED ON ANYTHING READ HERE. If he is the child born 14 February 1857 at Burgersdorp he is AUGUSTA LOUISA KOLBE’S SON and a grandson of the 1820 Settler; if he belongs to his father’s 1874 marriage he is no relation at all, and a man marrying in 1884 as a second son cannot be. THE DATES FAVOUR KOLBE AND THE DOCUMENTS DO NOT SAY IT.

augusta-louisa-kolbe.r: THE SETTLER'S FOURTH DAUGHTER HAS THREE DOCUMENTS AND THIS ARCHIVE HAD NONE OF THEM. A WILL, MADE IN 1868 AND FILED IN 1873: KAB MOOC 7/1/332 no. 205, “KOLBE, AUGUSTA LOUISA. WIFE OF COENRAAD JOHANNES OTTO WERDMULLER VAN ELGG” — which is the first document read here that ties her to that man by anything but a newspaper. A DEATH NOTICE, MOOC 6/9/145 no. 9981, 1873. And a LIQUIDATION AND DISTRIBUTION ACCOUNT, MOOC 13/1/299 no. 93, 1874, which means there was something to distribute. SHE DIED IN 1873 AND HER HUSBAND REMARRIED IN JULY 1874 — a year and a month, which is what a widower does, and which settles the question this archive left open yesterday about whose son Charles Andrew is. NONE OF THE THREE IS READ.

charlotte-anne-callaghan.d: 17 Feb 1891, Hoopstad, Orange Free State — aged 32
charlotte-anne-callaghan.r: ELDEST DAUGHTER OF HUGH CALLAGHAN, ESQ., OF ASHBY MANOR, district of Queenstown; married Charles Andrew Werdmuller on 13 February 1884. SEVEN YEARS LATER SHE WAS DEAD AT THIRTY-TWO, at Hoopstad, “after a long illness”, and a correspondent’s obituary in the Queenstown Free Press adds that she had arrived there only a few months before, in indifferent health, with a disorder of the heart that proved organic. SHE LEFT “A HUSBAND AND TWO LITTLE GIRLS”, and it is that line which lets the 1909 marriage notice call Amy a second daughter.

hits.text: They read exactly as a missionary's children's names should: scriptural, Latinate, chosen rather than inherited. And one of them travels. Frederik Fortunatus Kolbe (1839) becomes Frederick Fortunatus Barry (1863) becomes Frederik Fortsenatus Booÿsen (1899) — one name carried across three surnames and sixty years, degrading slightly at each handover. A library in Cape Town has been saying so in four words since 1985.

hits.text: This archive keeps the two apart, and says which is which. One name, three surnames, no blood tie proved between two of them Fortunatus It comes out of the London Kolbes and ends up on a Booÿsen born in the year the war began. Who When What they are to the name Frederik Fortunatus Kolbe of the London Kolbes The source of the name. Frederick Fortunatus Barry — Carried into the Barrys by the Kolbe marriage of 1850. Frederik Fortsenatus Booÿsen b. 1899 And into the Booysens, spelled with a diaeresis, in 1899. Ruben, a Schoeman name, travels the same way into the Barrys — Ruben Jacobus Josuah Barry. Two daughters, one name, eleven months apart The two Gertrudes Not a duplicated record. Two children, two death certificates, two cemeteries.

catharine-sophia-maria-kolbe.v: Catharine Kolbe (1853) · Catharine Sophia Maria Kolber (1848)
catharine-sophia-maria-kolbe.r: SHE IS WHERE THE NAME COMES FROM, and this archive had her down as “Catharine Kolbe” and nothing more. On 13 November 1848 she stood godmother at Graaff-Reinet to her sister Margaretha's son HENRY JAMES BARRY, entry 603, and the clerk wrote her out in full: CATHARINE SOPHIA MARIA KOLBER. ELEVEN YEARS LATER her sister named a daughter CATHERINE MARIA SOPHIA — the Kathleen Barry who married into this family — and the name then ran through four more generations and three more surnames. This archive had called it a Barry name. It is a Kolbe name, and it belongs to a woman who never married into the Booyzens at all. She is also godmother at Burgersdorp in 1853, two entries above her sister Mary Elizabeth's son.

mary-elizabeth-kolbe.v: Maria Elizabeth Kolbe, in her estate notice · Enslin
mary-elizabeth-kolbe.r: HER DEATH IS NOW DATED, AND SHE DIED WITHOUT A WILL. The Friend of the Free State, 23 October 1863, twice in two weeks: “Derwyl MARIA ELIZABETH KOLBE zonder testament na te laten is overleden en de nagebleven echtgenoot G.F. ENSLIN by brieve van administratie ter vereffening van haren boedel als executeur is aangesteld” — she had died INTESTATE and her husband was appointed executor of her estate. This archive had only “before 1867”, inferred. It is now BEFORE 23 OCTOBER 1863, from a notice her own husband placed. MARGARETHA'S SISTER, and the woman who married GEORGE FREDERICK ENSLIN — which is the whole answer to a contradiction this archive carried as Serious, that Margaretha appeared to marry Enslin while married to John Barry. It was resolved from Margaret Downing's 1867 death notice. The Burgersdorp register of 23 October 1853 shows it instead: the two sisters baptising a son each, two entries apart, on one page.

hits.text: It was resolved from Margaret Downing’s 1867 death notice , which lists among her children “Mary Elizabeth (dead) who was married to George F. Enslin” . The Enslin marriage belongs to Margaretha’s sister . Here are the two sisters, on one page, on one day, baptising a son each. Mary Elizabeth Kolbe with her Enslin, Margareth Kolbe with her Barry, two entries apart in the Burgersdorp register on 23 October 1853. The contradiction → And it puts them at Burgersdorp. The 1915 death notice says the marriage was at “Burghersdorp (probably)” — a son guessing, sixty-five years on, at something nobody had told him.

anna-van-der-merwe-of-burgersdorp.r: The third godparent at the 1853 Barry font, and the only one who is not a Kolbe. A VAN DER MERWE standing at a Barry christening at Burgersdorp — a surname this archive has been chasing on the entirely other side of the family, among the Booysens of Graaff-Reinet. Not connected, and set down so the coincidence is on the record.

william-barry.r: Found twice in one day. He came in on the 1915 death notice of his mother Margaretha Kolbe, estate 1291, which names NINE children where his father's names eight — and then the Burgersdorp doopregister produced his baptism: WILLIAM FREDRIK, born 23 August 1853, christened 23 October, godparents JOHN KOLBE, ANNA VAN DER MERWE and GEORGE KOLBE. Two of the three are his mother's brothers. A SECOND William Frederick Thomas was baptised in 1861 and this archive cannot say whether the first died or a clerk erred — a doubt re-surfaced, and briefly mistaken for a new find, when the index was asked for every Barry child of a Kolbe mother. He is not on his father's notice, not on the Cape Rebel roll, and nowhere else in this archive. His father's 1903 registration said ELEVEN children; with William there are nine named and two still missing.

alida-jacoba-van-ellinckhuizen.r: Wife of John Augustus Barry II and the mother of nine children baptised at Burgersdorp and Dordrecht between 1871 and 1889. This archive had John Augustus II as a name on two death notices with no wife and no children at all until the index was asked for every Barry child of a father called John Augustus. Her surname is spelled nine different ways across the entries — Ellinckhuizen, Ellinckhuisen, Elinchhiusen, Westerhuizen, Ellincahuyzen — and one son carries it as a forename. FROM THE INDEX.

john-augustus-barry-ii.r: THE ENTRY HAS NOW BEEN READ, film 008119684 image 876, and every witness at his font is a KOLBE: “Gt: JOHN KOLBE, MARGARET KOLBE, AUGUSTA KOLBE” — the third name is the least certain of the three. The clerk writes the child JOHN AUGUST and the mother MARGARETWINA KOLBE. Read beside his brother’s font of the following year, where the godmother is CATHARINE SOPHIA MARIA KOLBER, it makes one point twice: the forenames this archive has spent the project calling BARRY NAMES are Kolbe names, standing at Kolbe godparents’ fonts. The eldest son on the 1915 notice, carrying his father's name exactly — which is why this archive calls the father John Augustus Barry I. His own documents call him simply John Barry, and that is the third man in this family the name has to be shared out between. His birth date does one more job than it looks: being HARD, off a register, it is what forces his brother James Henry's “about 1847” to move.

He remains exactly what he was: an unresolved second William, indexed twice over to Graaff-Reinet and Dordrecht , eight years after the Burgersdorp baptism . On Henry Jaonas there is an argument, and it comes entirely out of figures this archive already held. John Augustus Barry II was born 13 March 1847 and baptised four weeks later — a documented date, off a register. James Henry Barry is carried in this archive as born "about 1847" , and that figure is not a register at all: it is an age worked back from his death at Barkly East on 23 June 1939. Two brothers cannot both be born in 1847 , and the approximate date is the one that has to give way.

johan-gottlieb-kolbe.v: John Gottlob · “JOHN GODLOFF KOLBE ESQ. OF BRUNSWICK-SQUARE”, in his son’s 1844 obituary · and twenty-four spellings in the Westminster rate books
johan-gottlieb-kolbe.tree: The 1844 obituary’s “Brunswick-square”. No Westminster rate book, land tax return, census or burial register places him there, and Bloomsbury’s own sources have not been searched.
johan-gottlieb-kolbe.r: HE HAD EIGHT SONS, AND THIS ARCHIVE KNEW OF ONE. His son’s obituary in the Grahamstown Journal of 19 December 1844 calls George Augustus “THE LAST REMAINING OF EIGHT SONS OF JOHN GODLOFF KOLBE ESQ. OF BRUNSWICK-SQUARE, LONDON”. SEVEN BROTHERS, ALL DEAD BEFORE DECEMBER 1844, none of them named anywhere in this archive — and dead men do not appear in a census, which is why the 1841 Conduit Street household holds three women and no sons. THE OBITUARY ALSO PUTS HIM AT BRUNSWICK SQUARE, in Bloomsbury, where the census and the death put him at CONDUIT STREET in Mayfair, a mile and a half away. Both can be true twenty years apart, and this archive has already moved this man once — off the family tree’s Lamb’s Conduit Street — so it records a second address rather than making a second correction. “ESQ.”, not “tailor”. AND HE IS IN THE LONDON GAZETTE, nine years before he died: issue 19424, page 1702, 29 September 1836, dissolving the copartnership of “JOHN GOTTLOB KOLBE and DAVID FLETCHER, of Conduit-Street, Bond-Street, in the County of Middlesex, TAILORS”. That is his trade, his street and a business partner, in print, from a free source — and it pushes him back to Conduit Street in 1836. AND THE DEATH IS NOW A GRO REFERENCE: FreeBMD gives one Kolbe death in all of England and Wales for 1845–46 — “Deaths Dec 1845, KOLBE, JOHN GOTTLOB, ST GEO HAN SQ, VOL 1, PAGE 35”. The district matches the census; the name form JOHN GOTTLOB matches his son's 1803 baptism; and the certificate, not yet ordered, would name the informant. FOUND IN THE 1841 CENSUS, which settles two things this archive had argued from other documents. He is at CONDUIT STREET, St George Hanover Square, sub-district MAY FAIR, aged 76 — four years before he died at number 34, and independent of the death record that corrected the family tree's Lamb's Conduit Street. And his birth county is entered as “FOREIGN”, which is the first document in this archive to say in its own words that he was not English. HO107, piece 734, book 1, folio 11, page 15, SCHEDULE 38. Three women share that schedule: Marianne, 35, Charlotte, 30, and Amelia A., 25. Tailor. Died at 34 Conduit Street, Mayfair — not Lamb's Conduit Street; the tree's photograph is of the wrong building. 16 SEPTEMBER 2026 — THE ADDRESS ARGUMENT IS OVER, AND HE HAD TWO WIVES. The WESTMINSTER RATE BOOKS index him ONE HUNDRED AND TWENTY-ONE TIMES between 1800 and 1831, under TWENTY-FOUR SPELLINGS of his forename — Gothel, Gotleb, Gotleib, Gotlieb, Gotliel, Gotlob, Gotlobe, Goltief, Gottieb, Gottiel, Gottlieb, Gottlob, Gutlieb, Kottieb, Gilliet and once “Jos Gottiel”. In 1800 he is at BROAD STREET NORTH, St James Piccadilly, folio 41 — which independently corroborates the printed 1799 list of 234 master tailors, “Kolbe, John, 18 Broad-street, Soho”. From 1811 to 1831 he is at CHURCH STREET SOUTH, ST ANNE’S SOHO, year after year, and the 1829 land tax return says the same. BRUNSWICK SQUARE APPEARS IN NO RATE BOOK, NO LAND TAX RETURN, NO CENSUS AND NO BURIAL REGISTER — those are Westminster sources and Bloomsbury would not be in them, so they cannot disprove it, but Soho 1800–1831, St George Hanover Square in 1841 and a death there in 1845 leaves no window for it. AND THE BURIAL IS NOW A REGISTER ENTRY RATHER THAN A TREE CLAIM: Westminster Burials, City of Westminster Archives Centre — DIED 18 NOVEMBER 1845, BURIED 26 NOVEMBER 1845 AT ST JOHN THE BAPTIST, GREAT MARLBOROUGH STREET, page 7, year of birth given as 1764. The date matches the tree’s “26 November 1845, entry 55, grave 7” to the day and the “7” matches; the church does not. HIS FIRST WIFE MARY DIED 2 AUGUST 1814 AGED 46 and his SECOND, ALSO MARY, DIED 15 AUGUST 1824 AGED 36, both buried in the German Lutheran Church register, TNA RG 4/4631 — which is why one Mary could never be made to fit a run of baptisms from 1792 to 1819. AND THE LONDON GAZETTE HOLDS FIVE NOTICES, NOT THE ONE THIS ARCHIVE HAD. 12 MAY 1824 — the partnership of JOHN GOTLOB KOLBE AND JOHN HENRY KOLBE, of CHURCH-STREET, SOHO, TAILORS, dissolved. 30 SEPTEMBER 1836 — Kolbe and DAVID FLETCHER of Conduit-Street dissolved. 21 MARCH 1845 — “JOHN GOTLIEB KOLBE AND RICHARD DAVIES, OF CONDUIT-STREET, BOND-STREET, TAILORS, HAS BEEN DISSOLVED BY MUTUAL CONSENT”, EIGHT MONTHS BEFORE HE DIED and still calling himself a tailor, which is what the obituary’s “Esq. of Brunswick-square” has to be set against. 1824 WAS THE YEAR IT ALL WENT: the partnership dissolved in May, his second wife dead in August, and his son in the insolvent debtors’ lists in October and November. 16 SEPTEMBER, LATER — AND THE 1799 TAILORS’ LIST HAS A TWIN. In APRIL AND MAY 1834 the London press printed the roll of “considerably more than THREE HUNDRED of the Master Tailors of the metropolis” who met at Willis’s Rooms, St James’s-street, to resist THE GRAND NATIONAL CONSOLIDATED TRADES’ UNION, and the entry reads “KOLBE AND FLETCHER, CONDUIT-STREET” — Morning Post 30 April, Globe 30 April and 10 May, Old England 4 May, Morning Herald 10 May, London Courier 10 May, True Sun 10 May, Public Ledger 12 May. SEVEN NEWSPAPERS, ONE LINE. IT CLOSES THE GAP: the rate books had him in Soho to 1831 and the Gazette at Conduit Street by 1836; HE WAS AT CONDUIT STREET, WITH FLETCHER, BY 29 APRIL 1834. AND IT RHYMES WITH THE FIRST LIST THIRTY-FIVE YEARS EARLIER — in December 1799 one of 234 masters over the Combination Acts, a young man at 18 Broad-street; in April 1834 a firm with a partner and a Bond Street address, seventy years old, on the masters’ side of the same argument.

hits.title: The Booyzen Archive
hits.text: What this archive has established The letter was changed on purpose Booyzen , not Booysen. The family says the spelling was changed during the Anglo-Boer War, to avoid being taken for men who fought on the British side — and the surname statistics agree with the family. The name → The Kolbes end in London, not the Cape Johan Gottlieb Kolbe died at 34 Conduit Street on 18 November 1845 and was buried at the German Savoy Church eight days later, aged 81. The line runs out of the Cape and into a German congregation in Mayfair.

charles-kolbe.r: ONE OF THE EIGHT SONS, NAMED FOR THE FIRST TIME. Father John, mother Mary. Batch C15051-2. HIS DEATH IS NOT IN THE GERMAN LUTHERAN REGISTER, which holds six other Kolbe burials — but a second son was christened CHARLES Samuel nine years later, and families reused a name when the first child carrying it had died. That is an inference and not a record.
charles-kolbe.tree: That he died before 1807. It rests on the reuse of the name, not on a burial entry.

john-henry-kolbe.d: 13 Apr 1832, buried 22 Apr 1832, German Lutheran Church
john-henry-kolbe.r: ONE OF THE EIGHT SONS, AND THE ONE WHO LIVED LONGEST OF THOSE FOUND. Baptised 29 July 1800, father John, mother Mary, batch I02559-1. TNA RG 4/4631 folio 100: died 13 April 1832, buried 22 April, AGED 32 — twelve years before the obituary that counted him among the seven already gone. AND HE SPEAKS. Old Bailey, session of 13 January 1819, trial t18190113-149 — Richard Kerr indicted for stealing “one coat, value 6l., the property of JOHN HENRY KOLBE”. His own deposition: “MY FATHER IS A TAILOR, AND LIVES IN CHURCH-STREET, SOHO. On the 9th of January, about eleven o’clock at night, I stopped at the Star and Crown public-house, Westminster, and left my coat over my horse’s head — I had a chaise standing at the door; I saw the prisoner go out, and suspected him — I went out, and missed my coat.” NOT GUILTY. HE WAS EIGHTEEN, and his brother George Augustus sailed for Algoa Bay the following year. It is the only voice this archive has from the Soho house, and it corroborates the rate books’ address from a source that had no interest in it. AND THE LONDON GAZETTE SAYS WHAT BECAME OF HIM. 12 MAY 1824, issue 18027 page 796: the partnership of “JOHN GOTLOB KOLBE AND JOHN HENRY KOLBE, OF CHURCH-STREET, SOHO, IN THE COUNTY OF MIDDLESEX, TAILORS” dissolved — father and son, in business together, at the address he gave the court five years earlier. Then 9 OCTOBER and 16 NOVEMBER 1824, issues 18069 page 1668 and 18080 page 1900, in the INSOLVENT DEBTORS lists, petitions to be heard at Portugal-Street, Lincoln’s-Inn Fields on 5 November: “KOLBE, JOHN HENRY (SUED AS HENRY KOLBE), FORMERLY OF NO. 22, NORFOLK-STREET, MIDDLESEX-HOSPITAL, AND LATE OF NO. 4, MANSFIELD-PLACE”. HE WAS TWENTY-FOUR, OUT OF THE FAMILY BUSINESS AND OUT OF SOHO IN THE SAME YEAR HIS STEPMOTHER DIED, and he was dead at thirty-two. AND HE MARRIED THREE MONTHS AFTER THE TRIAL: Westminster Marriages — JOHN HENRY KOLBE AND MATILDA FORD, 26 APRIL 1819, ST MARGARET WESTMINSTER, both of that parish. He was eighteen. A MARY ANN MARIA FORD KOLBE MARRIED AT WHITECHAPEL IN THE FIRST QUARTER OF 1847 — GRO index volume AZ, 840, page 16 — and “Ford” carried as a forename is how families carried a mother’s maiden name. SHE IS VERY PROBABLY HIS DAUGHTER. AND THE PRESS GIVES HIS TRADE, WHICH THE GAZETTE DID NOT. Law Chronicle, Commercial and Bankruptcy Register, 13 January 1825: “KOLBE John Henry, of Norfolk-street, Middlesex-hospital, LAST OF MANSFIELD-ST., KENTISH TOWN, TAILOR, DRAPER” — so he set up on his own account in his father’s trade, and the Gazette’s “Mansfield-Place” is Mansfield Street, Kentish Town. THE MAY 1824 DISSOLUTION WAS REPORTED IN AT LEAST SIX LONDON PAPERS, all of them putting HIS name first: “J. H. Kolbe and J. G. Kolbe, Church-street, Soho, tailors”.

frederick-kolbe-of-1816.v: NOT a son of Johan Gottlieb — and the second Kolbe household in Soho
frederick-kolbe-of-1816.r: RIGHT SURNAME, RIGHT PARISH, RIGHT DECADE, AND A GAP IN THE FAMILY'S OWN BAPTISM RUN EXACTLY THERE. He is not a brother. His father is GEORGE and his mother ELIZABETH, and his register batch is C72301-7 rather than the family's C15051-2 or C06236-1. HE WAS ONE CLICK FROM BEING MADE AN EIGHTH SON, and what stopped it was reading the parents' names on the transcript instead of the name, place and year in the result list. The same check threw out HENRY KOLBE, baptised at Southwark on 2 February 1800 — father Henry, mother Susannah. AND THE REJECTION TURNED OUT NOT TO BE A DEAD END. Morning Advertiser, 31 DECEMBER 1832: “LEFT HIS HOME, MONDAY, DECEMBER 10, FREDERICK KOLBE, ABOUT 16, DARK HAIR AND EYES, WITH AN IMPEDIMENT IN HIS SIGHT. Any information addressed MRS. KOLBE, NO. 18, GERRARD-STREET, SOHO, will be rewarded; if he will return, will…” — and a boy “about 16” in December 1832 is one baptised in December 1816. GERRARD STREET IS TWO STREETS FROM CHURCH STREET. THERE WERE TWO KOLBE HOUSEHOLDS IN SOHO AT ONCE, and every Soho Kolbe record on this site has to be read against that. Whether the two families were related is not known here.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: And what it does to Brunswick Square Brunswick Square is in Bloomsbury. It is not in Westminster and would not appear in any of these books, so they cannot disprove it. What they can do is close the gap: he is rated in Soho from 1800 to 1831, he is in the 1841 census at St George Hanover Square with Amelia A, Charlotte and Marianne Kolbe, and he dies in St George Hanover Square in 1845 . There is no window left for a Bloomsbury house. Conduit Street is in St George Hanover Square. The obituary is the odd one out. What a rate book is, and why it beat the directory. A trade directory lists the men who paid to be listed. A rate book lists everyone the parish could get money out of, every year, by street.

george-augustus-kolbe.r: HIS OBITUARY IS FOUND, eighteen days after the death: Grahamstown Journal, 19 December 1844. “DIED at his Farm, Wirtemberg, near the Orange River, December 1st, THE REV. GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE, aged 44 years, a man possessed of a most amiable temper, and of more than ordinary abilities. HE WAS THE LAST REMAINING OF EIGHT SONS OF JOHN GODLOFF KOLBE ESQ. OF BRUNSWICK-SQUARE, LONDON, has left a WIDOW AND TEN CHILDREN... he having been for many years engaged in RENDERING THEM MEDICAL ADVICE AND ASSISTANCE whenever called upon... HIS DISEASE WAS AN AFFECTION ON THE LUNGS.” EIGHT SONS, seven of them dead before December 1844 and not one in this archive. BRUNSWICK SQUARE, which is not Conduit Street and is a mile and a half from it. A MAN WHO DOCTORED A DISTRICT FOR THIRTY YEARS, where his own death notice says only “Agriculturist”. And a cause of death, after nearly a year ill. The notice also says 44 when he was 41, and ten children when this archive counts eleven living — it is the best kind of source and it is not a register. 1820 Settler — the Nautilus, Owen's party, Algoa Bay 14 Apr 1820. Married at sixteen on a sworn falsehood. Preached across the Orange River. His grandson could not name him in 1915. 15 SEPTEMBER — HE WAS AN LMS MISSIONARY, AND HIS FATHER WROTE TO HIM. The South African Library at Cape Town holds MSB751, the GA KOLBE COLLECTION, donated by Dr Jean Griffiths of Somerset West in 1985: “George Augustus Kolbe, PHARMACIST, 1820 settler, MISSIONARY, married Margaret Downing” and, on a second entry, “George Augustus Kolbe, 1802–44. LMS MISSIONARY.” IT CORROBORATES A MEMORY THIS ARCHIVE PUBLISHED THE SAME MORNING AS AN INFERENCE — John Montgomery's recollection of a BUSHMAN MISSION SCHOOL AT KOOLSKOP about 1824, where Colesberg now stands. Two sources with nothing to do with each other, agreeing. AND THE COLLECTION IS FOUR PHOTOCOPIED PAGES CONTAINING A LETTER OF 23 AUGUST 1830 FROM JOHAN KOLBE IN LONDON TO HIS SON ON HIS ORDINATION — the only known document connecting the tailor of Conduit Street to the settler of Colesberg, and very likely to carry a London address at the head of it.

hits.title: The Booyzen Archive
hits.text: What was searched → Why this archive exists In 1915 a man at Barkly East filled in his own mother's death notice. Where it asked for her parents' names, he wrote: "Father: Kolbe, thinks James was christian name . Mother: Unknown ." His grandfather was George Augustus Kolbe — who married at sixteen on a sworn lie in Shoreditch, sailed on the Nautilus in 1819 as an 1820 Settler , preached across the Orange River, and named a Karoo farm after the Württemberg his own father had left. His grandmother was Margaret Downing of London.

hits.title: The Barrys
hits.text: The 1820 Settler hypothesis does not survive arithmetic. He was born 8 June 1819 . The settler fleets sailed from late 1819 and reached Algoa Bay from April 1820. He cannot have been born on that voyage. But the family does have a documented 1820 Settler — his own father-in-law, George Augustus Kolbe , who sailed on the Nautilus from Gravesend on 3 December 1819. Inferred The likeliest reading is that a true settler story attached itself to the wrong branch.

hits.text: George Augustus Kolbe was born 7 December 1802 . On 20 January 1819 he was sixteen years and six weeks old . Margaret Downing was born 23 February 1803 ; she was fifteen years and eleven months . Under Hardwicke's Marriage Act of 1753 a minor under twenty-one could not marry by licence without a parent's consent.

hits.title: Method
hits.text: The rule was written for a good reason — to stop John Barry collecting every mention of John Barry Booyzen — and it was implemented as “delete the shorter man” rather than “let the longer name go first”. So the moment anybody added George Augustus Kolbe of Wakkerstroom , George Augustus Kolbe stopped existing as far as the build was concerned. Why it is worth a section The data was never wrong. Every record, every document, every citation was intact and on disk the whole time.

hits.title: Open Questions
hits.text: The single most important unopened door: it indexes Cape (KAB) and Transvaal (TAB) estate files and death notices , which is where a death notice for Willem Hermanus Booyzen would be found. Cape Archives (KAB), Master's Office (MOOC) — one reference is already in hand: MOOC 6/9/35: 7698 (1845) , the estate of George Augustus Kolbe. It has not been ordered or read. The Dutch Reformed Church registers for Graaff-Reinet, Cradock, Colesberg, Burgersdorp, Dordrecht and Barkly East — already the backbone of the tree's citations, but read only where FamilySearch has indexed them.

margaret-downing.d: 2_ Nov 1867, Burgersdorp — the day illegible on the stone
margaret-downing.r: THE ANSWER WAS ON A PHOTOGRAPH THIS ARCHIVE HAS HAD ALL ALONG. The Burgersdorp monument is on the Kolbe page, and the caption quoted it as far as “ALSO HIS RELICT MARGARET DOWNING…” AND STOPPED THERE. The stone goes on: “BORN IN LONDON 23 FEBRUARY 1803 AND DIED AT BURGHERSDORP 2_ NOVEMBER 1867.” HER BIRTH IS NOW A DATE — 23 February 1803, where this archive had “c. 1804” — AND THE DEATH IS SETTLED AT 1867. Her son’s obituary of 15 April 1868 said she had died “about three months since”, which would have been January 1868; it was nearly five months, and a journalist rounding is a journalist rounding. THE DAY IS A 2 AND A DIGIT THAT WILL NOT RESOLVE at any magnification, and is not guessed. The Cape estate ran on: MOOC 13/1/253 no. 2, “DOWNING, MARGARET, WIDOW OF KOLBE, GEORGE AUGUSTUS. LIQUIDATION AND DISTRIBUTION ACCOUNT”, 1869 — and she had made a WILL OF HER OWN in 1854, MOOC 7/1/295 no. 70, ten years after she was widowed. Married at fifteen in Shoreditch, signing with a mark. Died owning a house and a farm.

hits.title: The Booyzen Archive
hits.text: Mother: Unknown ." His grandfather was George Augustus Kolbe — who married at sixteen on a sworn lie in Shoreditch, sailed on the Nautilus in 1819 as an 1820 Settler , preached across the Orange River, and named a Karoo farm after the Württemberg his own father had left. His grandmother was Margaret Downing of London. Both of them lie under a cut-stone monument at Burgersdorp — names, London birthplaces, farm and dates carved into it — about forty miles from where that notice was written. The family forgot them inside seventy years, with the headstone still standing. And it had happened before, on the other side of the house.

frederik-fortunatus-kolbe.r: THE SOURCE OF THE FORTUNATUS NAME across three families — and, as of 14 September 2026, A MAN WITH A HOUSEHOLD. The Settler's tenth child, born at a mission station the year his father was working the Orange River. He married ELIZABETH JOHANNA DU TOIT, and eight of their children are in the Dutch Reformed registers: baptised at COLESBERG in 1863, 1865, 1868, 1873, 1876 and 1877, at HOPETOWN in 1870, and at BETHULIE in 1881. The eldest is a GEORGE AUGUSTUS, named for the grandfather who had been dead nineteen years. THEN THE HOUSEHOLD GOES NORTH: three of those children marry or die at WAKKERSTROOM in the eastern Transvaal, four hundred miles from the font. That is the second proof of the Wakkerstroom convergence, and it does not depend on a name — it is a family moving.

She is named at eight fonts across eighteen years, and her name holds steady at every one of them but Hopetown, where the clerk wrote Geertruida .

george-augustus-kolbe-of-wakkerstroom.r: THE SETTLER'S GRANDSON, CARRYING HIS NAME ENTIRE, and the man the Wakkerstroom Kolbes descend from. Baptised at Colesberg in the year of his uncle Frederick Fortunatus Barry's birth. Married MARTHA SOPHIA KLOPPER, who was seventeen, about 1885; their eldest, Maria Johanna, was born at Wakkerstroom in 1886. AND HIS STONE SETTLES THE IDENTIFICATION BEYOND ARGUMENT: “VADER — GEORGE AUGUSTUS — GEB. 29 JULIE 1863 — OORL. 28 SEPT. 1954”, which is the COLESBERG FONT DATE TO THE DAY. The 1902 POW record with residence Wakkerstroom is NOT HIS: the other George Augustus Kolbe of that town was born 2 October 1861 and was exactly forty through ten months of 1902, where this one was thirty-nine. Died at Wakkerstroom on 28 September 1954, aged 91, which counts EXACTLY from the Colesberg font: born 29 July 1863, dead 28 September 1954. He outlived two of his sons by thirty-six years.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: The correction → And the prisoner of war is decided, in the other direction. At breakfast this archive gave the 1902 POW record — WO 108/368 , age 40, residence Wakkerstroom — to the man born in 1863, on the strength of the residence. By lunch it had withdrawn that, because he was thirty-nine. The stones close it: the other George Augustus Kolbe of Wakkerstroom was born 2 October 1861 , and was therefore exactly forty from October 1901 to October 1902 . The prisoner is the elder man. Published, withdrawn and reversed inside one day, and all three are on the corrections page, because a reader is owed the whole of that and not just the answer.

hits.title: Method
hits.text: The rule was written for a good reason — to stop John Barry collecting every mention of John Barry Booyzen — and it was implemented as “delete the shorter man” rather than “let the longer name go first”. So the moment anybody added George Augustus Kolbe of Wakkerstroom , George Augustus Kolbe stopped existing as far as the build was concerned. Why it is worth a section The data was never wrong. Every record, every document, every citation was intact and on disk the whole time.

hits.title: The Kolbes
hits.text: He is baptised at Colesberg on 11 October 1863 — and he dies at Wakkerstroom , in the eastern Transvaal, on 28 September 1954, aged ninety-one . The age counts exactly from the font. In between he married Martha Sophia Klopper , who was seventeen; their eldest was born at Wakkerstroom in 1886; and he was dead at ninety-one before this archive existed. A prisoner of war, and this archive nearly gave him to the wrong man. WO 108/368 , the master list of Boer prisoners numbers 1–32561, holds a George Augustus Kolbe, aged 40, nationality Transvaaler, residence Wakkerstroom, prison Natal, 1902 .

george-augustus-kolbe-of-burgersdorp.r: THE SECOND GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE OF WAKKERSTROOM, and the reason this archive had to withdraw a claim within the hour. His stone: “IN LIEFVOLLE HERINNERING AAN ONS OUERS — GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE — GEB. 2 OKTOBER 1861 — OORL. 8 NOVEMBER 1934 — EN SUSANNA MARGARETHA KOLBE — GEB. 26 OKTOBER 1861 — OORL. 28 JULIE 1940 — HULLE RUS.” BORN AT BURGERSDORP, which is where the 1820 Settler is buried and where the Settler's twin son George Augustus was born in 1836; the descent is not documented here and is not claimed. He is buried at WAKKERSTROOM although he died at Standerton, in the same cemetery as the other man of his name, TWO YEARS APART IN BIRTH AND TWENTY IN DEATH. AND THE BIRTH DATE DECIDES THE PRISONER: the 1902 POW record of WO 108/368 gives a George Augustus Kolbe of Wakkerstroom AGED 40, and a man born 2 October 1861 was forty from October 1901 to October 1902, where the other was thirty-nine all year. THE PRISONER IS THIS MAN. 16 SEPTEMBER 2026 — THE POW ENTRY NOW HAS A FOLIO: TNA WO 108/368 FOLIO 709, the War Office list of Boer prisoners of war numbers 1–32,561, which records him as a TRANSVAALER, residence WAKKERSTROOM, and held in NATAL. He is one of SIX KOLBE MEN in that list, and the only one of the six not in the southern Free State.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: But the same farm carrying the same surname forty years apart is not nothing. The Settler’s own forenames, twice Two men called George Augustus Kolbe were taken prisoner in the same war — one at Wakkerstroom , one at Bethulie . The Wakkerstroom one was already identified on this site , from the gravestones, before this search was run: George Augustus Kolbe of Burgersdorp, born 2 October 1861 , who was forty from October 1901 to October 1902 where the other Wakkerstroom man of that name, born 29 July 1863, was thirty-nine all year. The folio number is the only thing this sweep added to him. The stones → The Bethulie man is new and unattached. No descent is claimed for him.

maria-johanna-kolbe.v: Maria Johanna Kolbe van der Merwe
maria-johanna-kolbe.r: HER STONE IS READ AND IT NAMES HER CHILDREN THE WAY THIS FAMILY ALWAYS DOES. “IN LIEFDEVOLLE HERINNERING AAN ONS MAMMIE — MARIA JOHANNA VAN DER MERWE (GEB. KOLBE) — 26 OKT. 1886 – 1 OKT. 1953 — Wat hy doen is wel gedaan.” And underneath, six household names: MARTZI · P.S. · JUDIE · PIETMAN · CHARL EN SUZAN. THE BIRTH IS NOW A DATE — 26 October 1886, where this archive had only the year — and THE SIX CHILDREN ARE NEW. This is the THIRD stone in this archive to list children by what they were called rather than what they were registered as: the Booyzens at Silverton, the Kolbes at Wakkerstroom, and now this. BORN AT WAKKERSTROOM AND DEAD AT WAKKERSTROOM, sixty-seven years apart, in a town her grandfather had never seen. Her 1953 estate file is the document that names the whole household: FATHER George Augustus Kolbe, MOTHER Martha Sophia Klopper, HUSBAND Charl Daniel van der Merwe. Her birthplace is entered as “Wakkerstroomn, Transvaal, Blanke Unie-burger” — the clerk's spelling, and the Union's category.

frederik-fortunatus-downing-kolbe.v: Frederik Fortunetus Daomig Kolbe, on his own marriage entry
frederik-fortunatus-downing-kolbe.r: THE MAN WHO PROVED THE CONVERGENCE. He carries BOTH of this family's Kolbe names at once — FREDERIK FORTUNATUS off his grandfather, DOWNING off a London marriage of 1819 — and a London surname has no business in the eastern Transvaal except through that wedding. Born seventy-two years after it. Married HESTER GERBINA SUSANNA JOUBERT at Volksrust at twenty-one, the clerk writing his second name as “Daomig”. Dead at Wakkerstroom on 2 November 1918, four months after his brother Daniel, which is the influenza.

hits.title: The Kolbes
hits.text: Elizabeth Johanna , baptised at Colesberg in 1876, marries John Charles Pattison there at twenty-one. In both cases the age on the marriage agrees with the font to the year. This is the second proof of the Wakkerstroom connection, and it is the better one. The first was a name: Frederik Fortunatus Downing Kolbe , born at Wakkerstroom in 1891, carrying a London surname that has no business in the eastern Transvaal except through a Shoreditch wedding of 1819. That was decisive but it was a single word on a single record. This is a household — a father, a mother, eight fonts in three towns, and three of the children turning up together at the far end. Names can be coincidence. A family moving is not.

angeline-kolbe.r: A WOMAN OF THIS NAME DIES AT WAKKERSTROOM IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WAR, and this archive cannot say who she is. Twenty-eight years old, female, surname Kolbe, registered at Wakkerstroom on 15 November 1900. SHE IS NOT THE VOLKSRUST CAMP GRAVE: that is a G.E. Kolbe aged 35, a different age in a different year in a different place, and the camp was barely open in November 1900. She is not on the list of Frederik Fortunatus's eight children either — too young for Martha Angelina of 1868, too old for Catharina Maria Louisa of 1873. A daughter-in-law, most likely. THE RECORD NAMES NO PARENTS, NO HUSBAND AND NO CAUSE.

martha-angeline-kolbe.r: HER STONE IS READ, AND IT TAKES BACK WHAT THIS ARCHIVE SAID THIS MORNING. “TER GEDACHTENIS VAN ONS GELIEFDE KLEINE — MARTHA ANGELINE KOLBE — GEBOREN 9 OCT. 1901 — OVERLEDEN 8 DEC. 1901 — HEBR. 6”, and cut across the base, the mason’s town: NEWCASTLE. IT STANDS IN WAKKERSTROOM MAIN CEMETERY, NOT AT VOLKSRUST. The index this archive read gives her burial as “Volksrust, Eastvaal District Council” — which is the DISTRICT, not the town, and Wakkerstroom lies inside it. WITH THE TOWN GOES THE CAMP: a family stone in a town churchyard, in Dutch, cut by a monumental mason twenty-five miles away in Natal, is not a camp burial, and this archive should not have gone near the word. She was sixty days old, she died in the middle of the war, and that is all that can be said. She carries the name of her great-aunt Martha Angelina, baptised at Colesberg in 1868.

hits.text: Daniel's death registration carries the words G A Kolbe's son , which the index mangled into G A Kolbelsson — and that misprint is the line that ties the graves to the old man. Two women the war took, and one this archive cannot name Angeline Kolbe , aged 28, died at Wakkerstroom on 15 November 1900 . Martha Angeline Kolbe , born 9 October 1901, died 8 December 1901, buried at Volksrust — sixty days old. Volksrust held a concentration camp, and this archive records the burial place without claiming the cause, because it has read no camp register that names the child. Angeline is not the camp grave NAAIRS holds — that is a G.E. Kolbe, aged 35 , a different age in a different year in a different town.

hits.text: The official record at the end of his life calls him simply an agriculturist , and he died on his own farm. Those are not contradictions — they are a life in sequence — but the archive should stop leading with "missionary". Ten children, and one who is missing The notice names ten. Julia Kolbe , whom MyHeritage flags as born two years after her father's death, is likewise absent, as she must be.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: DOROTHEA REGINA AND RUBEN JACOBUS JOSUAH ARE NOT ON IT, and this archive had both as children “named on the 1915 death notice”. They are grandchildren: a Dorothea Regina baptised at Slang River in 1892 and a Ruben Jacobus Hosea at Dordrecht in 1888, both to Henry Nicholas Barry and Anna Johanna Maria Schoeman. The page also gives Margaretha Kolbe's death as 2 AUGUST 1912, where this archive had only the year. And it says the marriage took place at “Burghersdorp (probably)” — a son of the house, writing in English with a solicitor's help, who did not know where his parents married and put it in brackets.

tersia-booyzen.r: Recorded the name-change and Anglo-Boer War account on the MyHeritage tree, as told to her by her father. It is FAMILY TESTIMONY AND NOT FROM A DOCUMENT — which is exactly why this archive quotes it in full and then tests it against the Cape Rebel rolls and the surname distribution, rather than repeating it.

hits.title: The Booyzen Archive
hits.text: It carries seven separate claims. None of them has yet been proved. Two are already in trouble, and three now have strong circumstantial support that did not exist before this archive was built.

hits.title: Disputed
hits.text: Documented He was not shot by anybody. The death registration → Inferred Three readings survive, and the archive does not choose between them: The generations are miscounted. Tersia Booyzen was counting from herself, not from the current researcher. Her "great great grandfather" may be a man this archive has not identified. "Shot and killed" is not an execution. It may mean killed in action, or shot during a farm clearance — neither of which would appear on the treason lists.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: This archive has not seen the medal, the ABO application, or Schroeder's signature. It is strong secondary evidence, and the prisoner number is what ties it to the register rather than to a name alone. The family's own war testimony now has something to be tested against. This archive has quoted Tersia Booyzen's account in full for the whole project and measured it only against surname distributions and rebel district figures, because there was no record. There is one now: a policeman of Pretoria who was at Talana in the first week of the war, wounded at Wagon Hill, present at Spion Kop and at the ZARPs' last stand, taken at Tolosberg with forty-one others and two guns, and shipped to India.

hits.text: The claim being tested "There were some Booysens who were joiners, fighting on the side of the British, so our great grandfather changed the spelling to Booyzen so as not to be associated with them." — family testimony recorded on the MyHeritage tree from Tersia Booyzen. The full account → Documented That a change happened is on the record twice over. MyHeritage carries "Former name: Booysen" as a formal Name Change fact on Willem Hermanus "William Henry" Booyzen (1851–1905) — and, far better, both spellings appear on a single sheet of paper in September 1905 .
